transmission. Beyond their role in brain structure, essential 
fatty acids (EFAs) are involved in the synthesis and functions 
of neurotransmitters and in the molecules of the immune 
system. Nutrition can impact multiple functions in most parts 
of the brain (see Box 41-1). 
Nerve cells communicate through the release of molecules 
of neurotransmitters from the transmitting (releasing) end of one 
nerve cell, through the synapse between them, to the receiving end 
(receptors) of a nearby neuron. There are numerous neurotrans-
mitters, including serotonin, acetylcholine, dopamine, norepi-
nephrine, epinephrine, and glutamate. Amino acids such 
as tryptophan, tyrosine, and glycine are examples of nutrients 
necessary to the formation of neurotransmitters (see Table 41-1).
